newsitem.title: USA: Pogo sees July Thai Gulf production rise.
newsitem.headline: Pogo sees July Thai Gulf production rise.

text.p: Pogo Producing Co said Tuesday Gulf of Thailand production, which began in February, should increase in late July as a third platform is brought into production.

The company also reported a doubling of first quarter profits to $12.8 million, or $0.38 per share, on revenues of $61.3 million, from $6.3 million, or $0.19 per share, on revenues of $48.1 million in 1996.
It said production volumes increased from 1996 levels, to 129.7 million cubic feet of natural gas and 13,903 barrels of crude of and condensate daily in 1997's initial quarter.
Chairman Paul G. Van Wagenen said, "We drilled rapidly during the first quarter with good success, both in the U.S. and in the Gulf of Thailand."

He also said "the aggressive $210 million capital and exploration budget approved by our board of directors earlier this year will allow us to continue to add significant new hydrocarbon reserves in 1997, following the all time high level of proven reserves we reached at year-end 1996."
Production at the Gulf of Thailand's Tantawan field began from the "A" and "B" platforms, with the "C" platform to be set and producing by late July, Pogo said.

Pogo said the "D" platform is now being built and will be installed in August and platform drilling will resume at that time. Production from "D" platform wells is expected to begin early in 1998. Additional platforms will be added as more successful development drilling on Tantawan is accomplished.
Concurrent with development drilling at Tantawan, Pogo said, successful exploratory drilling has been underway on the remainder of the 1.3 million acre Block B8/32 license.
The Benchamas area is now being developed and should come on production in the second quarter of 1999, it said.

In the Gulf of Mexico, the new East Cameron Block 334 "E" Platform began producing in early April, at about 145 million cubic feet of natural gas and 5,000 barrels of crude oil and condensate per day. These volumes are not included in first quarter results, it noted.
The company said it holds a 58.3 percent working interest in these new deep reserves.
The "F" platform has been ordered and should be set in the fourth quarter of 1997 with production from this one-slot, 42-percent-owned platform expected in late December.

Van Wagenen said, "A total of 33 wells are budgeted for the Gulf of Mexico this year, including nine which will be classified as exploration wildcats. These exploration wells should result in some important new reserves additions for Pogo." ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
Pogo is operator of the Thailand concession area where 50 wells have been drilled and 30 are planned for 1997. It and Rutherford-Moran Oil Corp have 46.34 percent working interests there.

With development drilling completed on "A" and "B" platforms, Pogo said, Tantawan field gross production rates are now at about 88 million cubic feet of natural gas and 6,300 barrels of crude oil and condensate per day.
Drilling of development wells for a third ("C") platform is underway with production expected to come on stream in late July.
